headline: Hijacked fridges, Zyxel switch exploits and APT signing flaws dominate the day
overview: Today's shows lead with attacks on critical systems, from European blood bank and supermarket refrigeration to a Zyxel switch zero-day that compromised nearly a thousand devices. Several episodes flag unpatched or end-of-life products and package-manager signature bypasses on Debian and Ubuntu. Election-day threats and the political fallout for AI infrastructure round out the news.

topStories.title: Refrigeration systems hacked in Europe
topStories.summary: Attackers disrupted refrigeration in European blood banks and supermarkets, affecting blood supply in France. Coverage ties these incidents together as a recurring threat to cold-chain systems.

topStories.title: Zyxel switch zero-day compromises about a thousand devices
topStories.summary: Attackers exploited Zyxel GS1900 switches via a pre-login flaw, stealing configurations and password hashes. Many devices still used factory passwords, and the exploit also worked on switches with the June patch, so updated firmware is advised.

topStories.title: APT29-linked attacks on outdated phones
topStories.summary: Russia-linked actors are using hacked websites to target out-of-date iPhones and Android phones, where simply visiting a page is enough. The advice is to enforce minimum OS versions in device management.

topStories.title: Linux and APT package integrity flaws
topStories.summary: A critical Linux kernel TCP flaw can allow remote root on some systems, while an APT signature bypass on Debian and Ubuntu can let attackers inject malicious packages, especially over HTTP. Patching and moving to HTTPS are recommended.

topStories.title: Critical patches and end-of-life products
topStories.summary: Cisco, WatchGuard, Barracuda and other vendors shipped critical fixes, while SonicWall will not patch unsupported GMS flaws. Teams are urged to patch quickly and remove internet exposure of unsupported systems.

topStories.title: Binance and French bank heists
topStories.summary: Large cryptocurrency and banking thefts were reported, with a Binance heist attributed to North Korea and a French bank heist estimated at about $133 million. Coverage also mentions fake job interviews used in the Binance case.

episodes.title: Claude, you've got company.
episodes.summary: Covers Claude Dispatch remote command risk, residential proxies on White House networks, airline breaches tied to an attack on Amadeus, critical Cisco and WatchGuard patches, GhostMap reboot loops on Android, and a Zyxel zero-day. Also includes a guest on the NIST post-quantum roadmap.

episodes.title: Ballots, bots, and backlash.
episodes.summary: Covers election-day voting system glitches and misinformation, hackers tampering with European refrigeration, questions over OpenAI security warnings, a roughly six-billion-dollar North Korean-attributed heist at Binance, and Barracuda critical patches. Includes an interview with Box's CISO on enterprise AI security.

episodes.title: Blood bank fridge hacks, Anthropic model identity, Google Calendar phishing
episodes.summary: Covers blood bank fridge attacks in Europe, Anthropic work on proving which AI model answered, Google Calendar phishing that hijacks sessions and bypasses MFA, a Chinese keyboard app used to deliver malware, a French bank heist of about $133 million, and APT29-linked attacks on unpatched phones.

episodes.title: SANS Stormcast Thursday, November 5th, 2026: Email Test Scripts; runZero oobscan BMC/IPMI; apt Signature Bypass (CVE-2026-109518); SonicWall GMS EOL Unpatched Flaws
episodes.summary: Covers abuse of test email scripts left on production sites, a new out-of-band scanning tool for exposed management interfaces, a critical APT signature bypass enabling malicious package injection over HTTP, and unpatched SonicWall GMS flaws on an end-of-life product.

episodes.title: Why a Data Center Slowdown Benefits Big Tech
episodes.summary: Discusses whether a slowdown in data center construction could benefit large tech firms after the election backlash, with headlines on ChatGPT search, a Meta acquisition and Apple AI spending limits. This is a general AI news show with no security focus.

episodes.title: How the Midterm Results Change AI
episodes.summary: Examines how the midterm results could affect AI scrutiny, data center construction and AI regulation, and suggests the backlash may produce better local community deals rather than halting AI buildout. General AI news, not security-focused.

episodes.title: That's Not Supposed to Happen - PSW #951
episodes.summary: Covers a range of security news including supermarket refrigeration attacks, a large Android TV botnet takedown, a Linux TCP flaw, the Binance theft, hacked emergency alert apps, and AI-assisted exploit development.

episodes.title: Zyxel 2nd Switch 0-Day, 1K Hacked, Debian/Ubuntu APT MitM Flaw, France Blood Supply Cyberattack
episodes.summary: Covers a second Zyxel switch zero-day that compromised about a thousand devices, a Debian and Ubuntu APT man-in-the-middle flaw, and the French blood supply cyberattack. The notes also mention AI-linked breaches and Chrome 157 fixes.

episodes.title: APT29-linked phone exploits, Zyxel patch bypass, White House proxy | Cyber Security News Nov 5
episodes.summary: Covers APT29-linked exploitation of outdated iPhones and Android phones via hacked websites, the Zyxel GS1900 switch exploitation and firmware advice, a DreamHost file manager credential exposure, the APT retry-based package swap, Xen hypervisor memory flaws, and residential proxy traffic leaving the White House network.

episodes.title: Hospital Diverts Ambulances, 5.7M Breached by a Phone Call, Town Pays $82K Ransom
episodes.summary: Covers ransomware that forced a New Mexico Level 1 trauma center to divert ambulances, a phone-based social engineering breach affecting about 5.7 million people at Marathon Health, and a town paying an $82K ransom. Aimed at business leaders.

episodes.title: How AI agents are spooking the banks
episodes.summary: Covers AI agents calling banks on users' behalf, a Florida man indicted over a ransomware recovery fraud, and a sponsored interview on AI-driven alert triage. The notes indicate the show also touches on Binance fake job interviews and GCHQ missing storage devices.

episodes.title: ARTEX for Everyone: What Widely Available AI Hacking Means for Defenders
episodes.summary: Discusses ARTEX, an openly available AI-powered penetration testing framework now seen in real intrusions, and defensive steps such as rotating exposed credentials and using AI-enabled red team tools. Sponsored by a vendor.

episodes.title: Stolen Entra app secrets, cPGuard update hijack, Binance fake interview | Cyber Security News Nov 4
episodes.summary: Covers stolen Entra app secrets used to sign in through MSPs, a CPGuard update channel hijack, Siemens Node-RED exploitation, WS_FTP and Barracuda patches, a Linux kernel TCP flaw correction, Chrome 157 fixes, and a forged GitHub commit. Practical patch and credential rotation advice throughout.

episodes.title: 🎙️ Linux Kernel TCP Use-After-Free Gives Remote Unauthenticated Root on Every Major Distribution, Barracuda Critical Flaws Allow Root Access to Security Appliances, Google Dismantles 1.3 Million Devi
episodes.summary: Covers a remote unauthenticated root Linux kernel TCP flaw, critical Barracuda flaws enabling root on security appliances, Google's takedown of a large Android botnet, Android November updates, and a password manager security incident.
